solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Noble German friend's resting place

parts.note: a friend is a pal, so the possessive friend's gives pal's
a grave is where the dead are laid to rest

explanation.surface: A German aristocrat's pal has been buried, and we are shown the tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in "friend's" is ignored: PAL'S becomes PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a count palatine, a historical title of German nobility.

clue.text: Food item not in the first section of the dictionary?

parts.note: something you have gone past is beyond it, no longer in it

parts.words: the first section of the dictionary
parts.note: a dictionary opens with the words under the letter A

explanation.surface: A food word you would not find among the dictionary's opening pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Being past A in the dictionary means not being in its first section, so the food splits as PAST A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta, such as spaghetti or penne, is a staple Italian foodstuff.

clue.text: Flier having drunk ale felt funny

indicators.note: funny here means peculiar or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An airman who had downed some beer felt odd.
explanation.walkthrough: "Flier" looks like a pilot; it is a printed handout.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier, or flyer, is a printed handbill handed out for publicity, the same thing as a leaflet.

clue.text: Make a reservation for dining? It's within reach

definitions.meaning: ... means able to be got at, accessible

explanation.surface: Booking a restaurant table is easy because one is close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Booking dinner means securing a table, and something getatable is accessible or reachable.

clue.text: Whizz with a speed in team moving east

parts.note: speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

indicators.note: moving means the letters of in and team are stirred into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Something fast racing alongside a quick team heading eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: "moving" rearranges the letters of 'in team' into ETAMIN. Whizz and speed are both British slang for this drug, so 'speed' looks like a second definition but is MPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Whizz is British street slang for the stimulant drug, also called speed.

clue.text: Partner of blind English females

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female; doubled, FF stands for females

explanation.surface: A sighted companion helps blind English women.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'eff and blind' is British slang for swearing a lot, so eff partners blind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'effing and blinding' pairs these two words as euphemisms for cursing.

clue.text: Soft-hearted man's a syrup provider

indicators.note: hearted means the soft letter is placed in the heart of the man

parts.note: man is male; the 's is read as 'is', a link
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow is the one who supplies syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: "Soft-hearted" reads as kindly, but it splits: P for soft goes in the middle of MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple syrup is tapped from the sap of the maple tree, which provides it.

clue.text: Old charmer admits reading the better half of Homer

indicators.note: admits means the word for the charmer lets the other letter in

parts.note: mage is an old word for a magician or enchanter
R is one of the three Rs: reading, writing, arithmetic

explanation.surface: An ancient enchanter confesses to reading Homer's finer parts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Homer" suggests the Greek poet; it is Homer Simpson, whose wife is Marge.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Simpsons, Marge is married to Homer, so she is his better half, a wife.

clue.text: Shot of dope prepared to keep warm

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged dope holds the warm word inside
prepared means the letters of dope are made up in a new form

parts.note: warm and hot are close enough to be synonyms

explanation.surface: A dose of drugs is made ready to stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: "prepared" rearranges dope as POED, and "to keep" holds the warm word inside it. "Shot" looks like a dose; it is the verb meaning photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot a picture is to photograph it, so shot is an informal synonym for this past tense.

clue.text: Sub-par performance I'd picked up, noticing a lot

parts.note: in golf an eagle is a hole played two strokes under par

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words I'd are taken by their sound

parts.note: said aloud, I'd sounds just like eyed

explanation.surface: A golfer recalls a fine score they had spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eagle-eyed is sharp-sighted and misses nothing, observant.

clue.text: Company having drink either side of dessert

indicators.note: either side of means the drink's letters flank the dessert

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a tart can be a sweet pastry served as dessert

explanation.surface: A firm's party includes drinks served around the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly founded business, a young company.

clue.text: Perhaps fox has itch in lots of yards

parts.note: fox fur is an example of fur, hence perhaps
to have an itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A fox is scratching itself in many back gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: "yards" looks like gardens; it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is a unit of 220 yards, many yards together.

clue.text: Grant a good deal, bagging pounds

indicators.note: bagging means seizing, so the deal's words close round the pounds

parts.note: a good deal means a lot
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A grant that is a bargain, collecting a lot of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant is to give or assign, which is what allot means, to apportion.

clue.text: Meat course stuffed with firm dates in the middle

indicators.note: stuffed with means the course is filled with the other letters

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central letter of the word dates

explanation.surface: A dish served with dates stuffed into the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: "in the middle" takes T, the centre of dates; "stuffed with" puts the firm and that T inside the course. Entrée is a main course in America but a starter in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecote is a boneless steak cut from between the ribs of beef.

clue.text: Resent the money pocketed by a criminal trader?

parts.note: the take is the money taken in, the takings
money pocketed by someone belongs to them, which of expresses
a fence is a dealer in stolen goods

explanation.surface: Feeling bitter about cash that a crooked dealer kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The takings of a fence reads as TAKE OF FENCE; a fence is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence is to feel hurt or annoyed, the same as to resent something.

clue.text: Go off from high point to the west

indicators.note: to the west means the word runs leftwards in this across answer

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Head down from a summit going westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that goes off spoils or decays, which is what rot means.

clue.text: Swing certain to be covered by The Stones?

parts.note: to rock is to swing back and forth
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A music fan is sure that a swing number will be covered by the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stones suggests the band; the definition reads them as plain rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockbound means hemmed in or surrounded by rocks, as a coast can be.

clue.text: British want servant on island in time for intense flogging

parts.note: want here means a lack of something
Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's servant on his island

explanation.surface: A British wish to have a servant on an island for a severe beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Flogging is British slang for selling, not whipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Friday is the shopping day after US Thanksgiving, known for heavy discounted selling.

clue.text: Nag rector over wrong money put in pot

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
a sin is a wrong
the ante is the stake put into the pot before a poker hand

explanation.surface: Pestering the parish priest about the wrong cash in the kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: "Nag" looks like a verb; it is an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosinante is Don Quixote's broken-down horse, the most famous literary nag.

clue.text: Come to strip off in field

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Players are asked to come and change out of their kit on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: "field" looks like a playing area; it is everyone taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: The field in a race or contest is the whole set of entrants taking part.

clue.text: How one feels astride red moped

indicators.note: astride means the mood's letters sit on both sides of the red

parts.note: your mood is how you feel
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary, a Red

explanation.surface: The feeling of sitting on a red scooter.
explanation.walkthrough: "moped" looks like the motorbike; it is the past tense of mope.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch about is to mope listlessly, so mooched and moped are synonyms.

clue.text: Support domestic worker having lost face

indicators.note: losing face here means the first letter, the front, is dropped

parts.note: a maid is a household servant

explanation.surface: Help for a housemaid who has been humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and support both mean help given to someone.

clue.text: Commended a pair of daughters fencing in bog

indicators.note: fencing in means the first letters surround the bog like a fence

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; two give DD
mire is boggy ground

explanation.surface: Praise for two daughters who fenced off a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend is to praise, and admired here means praised or approved of.

clue.text: Place for novel caution by quiet, fantastic creature

parts.note: a referee books a player when cautioning them
sh is the call for quiet
an elf is a creature of fantasy

explanation.surface: A strange warning given by a silent, fabulous being.
explanation.walkthrough: "novel" reads as an adjective meaning new; it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookshelf is where books, novels included, are kept.

clue.text: French scorer gets Arsenal's third with a draw

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word Arsenal

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match

explanation.surface: A French striker nets Arsenal's third goal in a drawn game.
explanation.walkthrough: "scorer" suggests a footballer; it is a composer of musical scores. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, and a composer writes scores.

clue.text: Wanderer compos mentis in Scotland?

indicators.note: in Scots the word for not is often no, so the Scottish version replaces one word

parts.note: compos mentis means of sound mind, not mad

explanation.surface: Is a roaming Scot of sound mind?
explanation.walkthrough: Scots say 'no' for 'not' (as in 'I'm no sure').
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a person with no fixed home who roams from place to place.

clue.text: Backer of party with not a single Republican

parts.note: a do is a party
no means not a single one

explanation.surface: A party funder with no Republicans at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money in support, so is a backer or financial supporter.

clue.text: Article in Le Monde, with issue for free

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, as found in Le Monde, a French newspaper
a hitch is a problem or issue

explanation.surface: A French newspaper story whose edition is handed out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: "free" looks like an adjective meaning gratis; it is a verb meaning release.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch something is to unfasten it, to set it free.

clue.text: Fried food unwrapped with it

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer letters, the wrapping, are taken off

parts.note: chips are fried potato strips

explanation.surface: Fried food taken out of its paper and eaten with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips are traditionally wrapped in paper; here the wrapping is the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip is slang for fashionable or trendy, the same as being with it.

clue.text: Working in new club, not needing to be pressed

indicators.note: in means the working word is placed inside the new club

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Active in a new golf club, and needing no persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: "pressed" looks like urged or persuaded; it means ironed.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-iron fabric does not need ironing, that is, pressing, to look smooth.

clue.text: Italian dignitary once scoffing last of cold duck

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so the dignitary takes the letter inside

parts.note: the doge was the elected ruler of Venice or Genoa

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word cold

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler eats up the last bit of cold roast duck.
explanation.walkthrough: "duck" looks like the bird being eaten; it is a verb meaning evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question is to evade it, which is to dodge it.

clue.text: Person claiming money on spurge, occasionally

indicators.note: on means the money comes after, following the pick from spurge
occasionally means taking only some of the letters, every other one, of spurge

parts.note: legal tender is money

explanation.surface: Someone asking for cash to spend on a garden weed now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurge is a weedy plant; taking its even letters gives PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is someone who claims a title, especially a throne, often without right.
